newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland to host Bosnia police pledging talks.
newsitem.headline: Ireland to host Bosnia police pledging talks.

text.p: Forty-one nations are to meet in Ireland in late September in an effort to help build a police force to guide Bosnia's transition from war to peace.
Irish Foreign Affairs Minister Dick Spring said in a statement on Wednesday the Dublin government would hold "this important pledging conference" on behalf of the United Nations.
"The aim of the conference is to raise funds and contributions in kind for a comprehensive programme to restructure the police forces in the two entities of Bosnia and Herzegovina," he said.

"The development of democratic policing in that country is an important challenge and is essential to the process of consolidating peace and advancing the objective of creating self-sustaining stability in the region."
The talks are expected to focus on the need to train a new police force now that the bitter ethnic fighting which marked the breakup of Yugoslavia has given way to an uneasy peace.
Representatives of the Nato-led IFOR peace force in Bosnia together with the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) will also be present.
The conference is to be chaired by the U.N.'s Under Secretary-General for Peacekeeping, Kofi Annan, and the International community's High Representative for former Yugoslavia, Carl Bildt.
